items.question: Where must the supreme beloved goddess be ritually established?
premises: The rite specifies a locus of placement.
The locus is the thousand-spoked great lotus.
The supreme beloved woman is the object placed there.
items.inference: The supreme beloved goddess must be established in the thousand-spoked great lotus.
uncertainties: Whether sahasrāra refers to a bodily center or an external diagram is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Having placed the supreme beloved woman in the thousand-spoked great lotus.

rows.grounds: injunctive or optative sense of offering

items.question: To whom should external worship and related offerings be presented?
premises: The rite prescribes an act of offering.
The offerings include external worship and so on.
The specified locus is the deity's right hand.
items.inference: External worship and related offerings should be presented into the deity's right hand.
items.plain_english: One should offer external worship and the rest into the right hand of the deity.

rows.grounds: locative compound indicating where splendors are

items.question: What condition places all splendors of recitation in the deity's hand?
premises: Recitation possesses all its splendors.
These splendors may be located in the deity's hand.
The verse states this as a condition addressed to the beloved.
items.inference: If all splendors of recitation are in the deity's hand, a further consequence follows.
uncertainties: The apodosis is completed in the following verse.
items.plain_english: O beloved, if all the splendors of recitation are in the deity's hand.

rows.grounds: refers to the recitation or its splendor

items.question: What need remains for separate worship or recitation when splendor is already offered?
premises: The prior condition places recitation's splendor in the deity's hand.
The verse questions the need for worship.
The verse questions the need for recitation.
items.inference: When recitation's splendor is already given to the deity, separate worship and recitation become unnecessary.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O beautiful-faced one, what need is there then for worship of that, or for recitation?

rows.grounds: compound indicating splendor of that mantra

items.question: What result arises from reciting the knowledge-mantra addressed to the goddess?
premises: The practitioner should recite the knowledge-mantra.
Recitation is directed as a prescribed act.
A splendor arises from that recitation.
items.inference: Reciting the knowledge-mantra produces its splendor.
uncertainties: vidyāmantra may specifically refer to the śrīvidyā mantra.
items.plain_english: O goddess, one should recite the knowledge-mantra, and its splendor is produced.

items.question: Into whose hand must the produced splendor especially not be offered?
premises: An offering act is under consideration.
The goddess's hand is named as a possible locus.
The instruction explicitly negates offering there.
items.inference: One must especially not offer that splendor into the goddess's hand.
uncertainties: The object not to be offered is implied from the previous verse as the mantra's splendor.
items.plain_english: O tremulous-eyed one, one should especially not offer it into the hand of the goddess.

items.question: What deficiency invalidates an offering made to the deity?
premises: An offering to the deity is considered.
The living principle may be absent from that offering.
The verse frames this absence as a condition.
items.inference: An offering made to the deity without the living principle is deficient.
uncertainties: The precise referent of jīvatattva is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: O goddess, if one offers to the deity without the living principle.

items.question: What kinds of material offerings should be presented to the deity?
premises: The verse names fragrance, flowers, and so on.
It extends this to whatever offerings there may be.
All such items are to be offered to the deity.
items.inference: All material offerings such as fragrance and flowers should be offered to the deity.
items.plain_english: Whatever there is, such as fragrance, flowers, and so on, one should offer all of it to the deity.

items.question: To which divine recipients should the splendor be offered?
premises: The splendor is the object of offering.
The goddess is named as a recipient.
The god is named as a recipient.
items.inference: The splendor should be offered to both the goddess and the god.
items.plain_english: O beautiful-hipped one, if one offers the splendor, one should offer it to the goddess and to the god.

items.question: What consequence follows for one who properly offers the splendor?
premises: Someone offers the splendor.
The act is affirmed as properly done.
A return or coming again is mentioned as consequence.
items.inference: For one who offers the splendor, there is a return or re-entry of that splendor.
uncertainties: The exact sense of punarāgamanaṃ in this ritual context is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: O goddess, O beloved, for one who indeed offers the splendor, there is its return.

items.question: Who wrongly experiences fear regarding the offered splendor's return?
premises: Fear may arise in this context.
Such fear is described as in vain.
The lowest type of person produces this fear.
items.inference: Only an ignorant person makes baseless fear about the splendor's return.
items.plain_english: O beautiful-hipped one, the lowest of men makes fear in vain.

rows.grounds: compound locative indicating where splendor enters
compound referring to the offered splendor
movement or absorption into deity's splendor

items.question: Where does the offered splendor ultimately come to rest?
premises: The splendor has been offered.
A locus is named as the midst of the deity's splendor.
The splendor enters that locus.
items.inference: The offered splendor enters into the midst of the deity's splendor.
items.plain_english: O beloved, that splendor indeed enters into the midst of the deity's splendor.

items.question: How is the living principle characterized in this concluding instruction?
premises: The speaker declares something has been told.
The subject told is the living principle.
It is described as very hard to obtain.
items.inference: The living principle taught here is declared to be very hard to obtain.
items.plain_english: O goddess, this living principle, very hard to obtain, has been told to you.

items.question: Who is enjoined to hear this tantra for its promised effect?
premises: This tantra is presented as something to be heard.
The hearer is identified as a practitioner.
The instruction is given as a prescription.
items.inference: The practitioner should hear this tantra.
items.plain_english: O beautiful-hipped one, O beloved, the practitioner should hear this tantra.

rows.grounds: locative particle referring to this matter

items.question: What immediate result follows when the practitioner hears this tantra?
premises: Hearing this tantra is the prior condition.
Success arises immediately and suddenly.
The verse denies any doubt about this.
items.inference: Hearing this tantra immediately brings success without doubt.
items.plain_english: Then indeed success arises suddenly; there is no doubt about this.

items.question: What status does one attain after reciting in relation to the beloved woman?
premises: Recitation involving the beloved woman is performed.
This act follows the prior teaching.
A lordship over all successes is named as result.
items.inference: After such recitation one becomes lord of all successes.
uncertainties: The exact ritual sense of reciting the beloved woman is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: Then indeed, having recited the beloved woman, one becomes the lord of all successes.

items.question: Under what mistaken condition might one recite during an eclipse?
premises: Recitation during an eclipse is prohibited.
Ignorance may lead to violation.
A dull-minded person is the agent of such violation.
items.inference: A dull-minded person might recite during an eclipse only out of ignorance.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, one should not recite during an eclipse; if a dull-minded person does so, it is from ignorance.

rows.grounds: compound referring to lunar eclipse occasion
compound referring to solar eclipse occasion
gerundive indicating what must not be deliberated

items.question: Should lunar and solar eclipse occasions ever be treated as negligible?
premises: Lunar and solar occasions are named.
The verse states they are not to be considered in some way.
The negation applies at any time.
items.inference: Lunar and solar eclipse occasions must never be disregarded or treated lightly.
uncertainties: The exact force of vicāryaṃ here may mean not to be deliberated away or not to be ignored.
items.plain_english: The lunar occasion and the solar occasion should never be disregarded.

rows.grounds: compound for prior merit or duty

items.question: What loss occurs if one neglects the proper observance of eclipse occasions?
premises: A higher dharma may be set aside in concession.
Previous dharma is named as subject to loss.
That previous dharma is destroyed.
items.inference: Neglecting proper observance destroys previously accumulated dharma.
items.plain_english: Let the higher dharma be as it may; the previous dharma is destroyed.

items.question: What enduring condition afflicts one who violates the eclipse observance?
premises: The person in question suffers consequences.
He becomes full of all calamities.
He also becomes full of all sins always.
items.inference: Violating the observance leaves one continually full of calamities and sins.
items.plain_english: He becomes full of all calamities and also always full of all sins.

rows.grounds: compound referring to solar eclipse occasion

items.question: What spiritual attainment results from properly observing the solar eclipse occasion?
premises: The solar occasion is to be observed.
Proper observation is prescribed.
Liberation is named as the result.
items.inference: Properly observing the solar eclipse occasion leads to liberation.
items.plain_english: O goddess, likewise, having observed the solar occasion, one obtains liberation.

items.question: What mistaken deliberation could lead one to avoid viewing the eclipse?
premises: Deliberation about the eclipse is considered.
The verse states a condition of not seeing the eclipse.
The instruction warns against this outcome.
items.inference: One should not, through deliberation, decide not to see the eclipse.
uncertainties: The protasis and apodosis relation is clarified by the next verse.
items.plain_english: O tremulous-eyed one, if, after considering, one does not see the eclipse.

rows.grounds: compound naming lunar and solar eclipse with connective

items.question: How should one respond to the occurrence of lunar and solar eclipses?
premises: Lunar and solar eclipses are the objects in question.
The prior verse warns against not seeing them.
Effortful observation is prescribed.
items.inference: Therefore one should carefully observe the lunar and solar eclipse.
items.plain_english: Therefore one should observe the eclipse of the moon and sun with effort.

rows.grounds: compound indicating duration from beginning to end of eclipse

items.question: What attainment follows from reciting throughout the entire duration of an eclipse?
premises: Recitation is performed during the eclipse.
The duration spans from initial seizing to final release.
Lordship of success is named as the result.
items.inference: Reciting from the beginning to the end of the eclipse makes one lord of success.
items.plain_english: Having recited from the beginning of the eclipse to its release, one becomes the lord of success.
